diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that if $|\supp_{\delta}(\bm q_n^{*})|>n(n+1)/2$, the corresponding $R_iR^\top_i, i\in\text{supp}_{\delta}(\bm q^{*}_n)$ are linearly dependent.

issues.failure_explanation: More than n(n+1)/2 matrices R_iR_i^T are linearly dependent, which gives a direction a with sum_i a_i R_iR_i^T/(w sigma^2) = 0. That leaves U(p) unchanged, but moving along a keeps ||q||_1 = 1 only if sum_i a_i = 0, and nothing guarantees this. Linear dependence alone yields only the Caratheodory-type bound n(n+1)/2 + 1. Reaching (n^2+n)/2 needs an extra argument, for example that optimality forces sum a_i = 0 or a rescaling argument. The proof also assumes U(p) is invertible on all of P_m(delta), which fails at delta = 0, although the lemma claims delta in [0,1/m].

failure_location.quote: Applying a perturbation argument for $\bm q^{*}_n$ along $\bm a$ yields another optimal solution that has a smaller $\delta$-support.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the short argument that at an optimum any perturbation direction satisfies sum a_i = 0 (otherwise rescale to strictly reduce H), or weaken the bound to n(n+1)/2 + 1. Restrict the finiteness claim at delta = 0 to feasible p with U(p) invertible.
issues.overall_effect: The stated sparsity bound (spt), and the later remark that only a fixed number of points are used when delta = 0, are not established as written.
issues.title: Support-size argument ignores the sum-to-one constraint
issues.why_classification: A short local argument or a one-unit weakening of the bound repairs it. The method and conclusions survive.

issues.failure_explanation: Step (tpo) needs ||(V^T W V)^{-1}||_2^2 <= 3/2. The only fact invoked is cond(V^T W V) < 3/2, which is a different quantity. On the event A the eigenvalues of V^T W V lie in [0.81, 1.21], so ||(V^T W V)^{-1}||_2^2 <= (1/0.81)^2 ≈ 1.52 > 3/2. The displayed constant is wrong and the inference is not valid as written. The same bound is reused for the q*_n case via (123511).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use ||(V^T W V)^{-1}||_2 <= 1/0.81 directly and carry the resulting absolute constant.
issues.overall_effect: Only the explicit constants (3/2, 2, 4) are affected. The conclusions are stated with the symbol ≲, so they survive.
issues.title: Inverse-norm bound derived from a condition-number bound
issues.why_classification: It is a routine constant correction that leaves every ≲ statement intact.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:main requires m ≳ n log n, so m n^2 ≍ n^3 log n, not n^3 log^2 n. The stated complexity does not follow from the cited sample-complexity estimate.

failure_location.quote: which has complexity $\mathcal O(mn^2)=\mathcal O(n^3\log^2 n)$ based on the error/sample complexity estimate in Theorem \ref{thm:main}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace O(n^3 log^2 n) by O(n^3 log n).
issues.overall_effect: The quoted complexity figure is off by a log factor. The comparison with the L x n least-squares cost is unaffected in substance.
issues.title: Wrong complexity exponent in the computational-cost remark
issues.why_classification: It is a one-line arithmetic correction with no effect on the argument.

issues.failure_explanation: G(p) is the trace of V^T W^{1/2} Sigma W^{1/2} V, not the MSE of the unweighted estimator. By (eq1) that MSE is only bounded by ||(V^T W V)^{-1}||^2 G(p). Gauss–Markov gives H(p*) <= MSE(p*), so H(p*) <= ||(V^T W V)^{-1}||^2 G(p*), which exceeds G(p*) in general. The deduction E_X[H(q*)] <= E_X[G(p*)] is therefore unsupported. It also takes an expectation over all X without conditioning on A.

failure_location.quote: so that $H(\bm q^{*}_n)\leq H(\bm p^*_n)\leq G(\bm p^*_n)$ (the first inequality follows from the definition of $\bm q_n^*$ and the second uses the Gauss--Markov theorem)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the inequality up to the factor ||(V^T W V)^{-1}||_2^2 <= 1.53 on A, with the expectation conditional on A.
issues.overall_effect: The assertion that case (p1-2) has estimation-variance term no worse than case (p1-1) holds only up to a constant and only on A.
issues.title: H(p*) ≤ G(p*) claimed via Gauss–Markov although G omits the (V^T W V)^{-1} factors
issues.why_classification: A constant factor and a conditioning statement repair it. The qualitative conclusion is preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound (tired) contains the extra term (1/m)||sigma||^2_{L^2_mu}. The remark asserts it is comparable to ||sigma sqrt(Phi_n/n)||^2_{L^1_mu} and hence dominated by ||sigma||^2_{L^2_nu}. No argument is given. Phi_n/n can be arbitrarily small where sigma is large, so (1/m)||sigma||^2_{L^2_mu} can exceed both the L^1 term and ||sigma||^2_{L^2_nu} (compare the displayed Jensen chain). Jensen only controls the L^1 term. The improvement over Theorem thm:cm17 is therefore not shown for arbitrary V_n.

failure_location.quote: Thus, \eqref{newb} improves the bound in Theorem \ref{thm:cm17} in terms of sample complexity.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the extra term in the comparison, or state an explicit condition under which (1/m)||sigma||^2_{L^2_mu} ≲ ||sigma sqrt(Phi_n/n)||^2_{L^1_mu}.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised improved sample complexity (newb) is proved only under an unstated condition, for example that Phi_n/n is bounded below on the support of sigma, or that the extra term is small.
issues.title: Unjustified equivalence in the claimed sample-complexity improvement
issues.why_classification: Adding a local condition or keeping the extra term preserves the method and the typical-regime conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The boosting argument needs l disjoint blocks of size k with l >= ceil(log(1/delta)/log 2), so n >= l k. The proof itself gives l < 3 log(1/delta) (via 2/log 2 < 3), which supports a hypothesis of order n > 3 log(1/delta) k. With only n > 1.5 log(1/delta) k the ceiling can fail: delta = 0.3, k = 10, n = 19 allows only one block, hence probability only 1/2. For delta close to 1 the hypothesis even permits n < k.

failure_location.quote: Choosing $l\geq \log(1/\delta)/\log 2$ and noting $2/\log 2<3$ yields the desired result.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the hypothesis to n >= 3 log(1/delta) k, with delta <= 1/2.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem is not proved under its stated sample-size hypothesis, only under a roughly twice larger constant.
issues.title: Hypothesis constant 1.5 in Theorem rb does not match what the proof yields
issues.why_classification: Only the numerical constant in the hypothesis changes. The result and proof architecture are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is stated for every r in N, but for r = 1, log r = 0, so k = 0 and V-bar_{n,0} = {0}. The bound would then claim ||f|| <= 24 sqrt(tau_2) for arbitrary f. If K has rank one (tau_2 = 0) and f ≠ 0, this is false. In the proof, s = c' r (log r)^3 = 0 contradicts s > 2r + 1, and the truncation and Chernoff parameters degenerate. More generally k ≥ r is not guaranteed for small r, whereas at least r + 1 functions are needed.

failure_location.quote: with $k = \lceil C_1 r(\log r)^3\rceil$ and for any $\delta>0$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (log r)^3 by (log(r+1))^3, or by max{1, log r}^3, or require r >= 2, and check that s > 2r + 1 holds.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem holds at best for r >= 2, or with log r replaced by something positive. The statement over all r is false.
issues.title: Theorem 984 false or ill-defined for r = 1 (k = 0)
issues.why_classification: It is a degenerate-case fix; the rate and method are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Since zeta = xi - xi', P(|zeta|>T) <= 4 e^{-T^2/4} under the subgaussian tail with c = 1. A union bound over s r entries gives at most 4 s r e^{-T^2/4}. With T >= 2 sqrt(log(sr)) this is only <= 4, not <= 0.1. The tail in (yonghuo) is likewise applied to zeta, although the assumption is stated for xi. The matrix Chernoff display also bounds P(lambda_min >= 0.5 s) instead of P(lambda_min <= 0.5 s), the wrong direction for the conclusion drawn.

failure_location.quote: Under the tail assumption \eqref{subexp}, it follows from a union bound estimate that, with probability at least $0.9$, for all $i\in [s]$, $\bm\zeta_{i} = \widetilde{\bm\zeta}_{i}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take T >= 2 sqrt(log(40 s r)), account for the doubled tail of the difference, and state the Chernoff bound for the lower tail. Check that the later estimates still hold; they do up to constants.
issues.overall_effect: The step giving lambda_min(L^T L) >= s/2 with probability 0.4, and hence the constant-probability bound with 24 sqrt(r tau_{r+1}), is not established as written. The order r (log r)^3 is unaffected.
issues.title: Truncation union bound does not give probability 0.9 with the chosen T
issues.why_classification: Only absolute constants in T change, and T remains of order log r. All later steps are unaffected.
